source_text:
Pricing is an annual institutional subscription. Eight thousand for a single department, twenty thousand for a faculty, forty-five thousand campus-wide. 

We charge twelve thousand per institution and expect eighty percent renewal. None of this is validated.

EpistemicOS evaluates manuscript claims. This happens before external review.

Business schools are the assumed primary buyer. They allocate budget through the research dean.

The faculty tier is twenty thousand. Deans approve most software purchases. Anything above that needs the finance committee.

I would never pay twelve thousand for this. My whole training budget is eight thousand.

We are leaning toward per-institution pricing, though nothing is signed.

The core problem is not writing quality. The core problem is whether claims withstand epistemic scrutiny. Its unit of analysis is the atomic manuscript claim, not the manuscript as a general text object.

All figures below are per institution per year. Setup is two thousand, support is three thousand, training is one thousand.

Our Spanish customers pay in euros. The US pilot is priced in dollars.
